Niddesa 2.1 Cittuppādakaṇḍa (The Section on the Arising of Consciousness)
2.1.8. Supramundane Resultant: The First Path Resultant 2.1.8.1.
The Pure Way Which phenomena are indeterminate (*abyākata*)?
At whatever time one develops supramundane jhāna that leads to liberation, which goes toward the waning of existence,
for the abandoning of views and for the attainment of the first stage— being quite secluded from sensual pleasures … [as before] … entering and dwelling in the first jhāna,
which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge— at that time there is contact … [as before] … there is non-distraction … [as before].
These states are wholesome.
As the result of that same supramundane wholesome jhāna having been performed and cultivated, secluded from sensual pleasures...
[as before] ...he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult to practice, slow in comprehension, and empty.
At that time there is contact … [and so on] … there is the faculty of final knowledge … [and so on] … there is non-distraction … [and so on] … these states are indeterminate.
Which states are indeterminate?
At whatever time one develops supramundane jhāna that leads to liberation and results in the diminution of formations,

which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge— at that time there is contact … [as before] … there is non-distraction … [as before].
These states are wholesome.
Through the performance and development of that very same supramundane wholesome jhāna, as its result,
secluded from sensual pleasures … [as before] … he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult to practice, slow in higher knowledge, signless.
At that time there is contact … [and so on] … there is the faculty of final knowledge … [and so on] … there is non-distraction … [and so on] … these states are indeterminate.
What states are indeterminate?

the third jhāna … the fourth jhāna … the first jhāna … [and so on] … 1075. “‘I shall enter and dwell in the base of infinite space, having completely transcended the base of infinite consciousness, perceiving “space is infinite”’: this too is a certain case where one who possesses right view does not fall away from it after death, when the body breaks up. 1076. “‘I shall enter and dwell in the base of infinite consciousness, having completely transcended the base of infinite space, perceiving “consciousness is infinite”’: this too is a certain case where one who possesses right view does not fall away from it after death, when the body breaks up. 1077. “‘I shall enter and dwell in the base of nothingness, having completely transcended the base of infinite consciousness, perceiving “there is nothing”: this too is a certain case where one who possesses right view does not fall away from it after death, when the body breaks up. 1078. “‘I shall enter and dwell in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, having completely transcended the base of nothingness’: this too is a certain case where one who possesses right view does not fall away from it after death, when the body breaks up. 1079. “‘I shall enter and dwell in the cessation of perception and feeling’: this too is a certain case where one who possesses right view does not fall away from it after death, when the body breaks up. 1080. “When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda asked the Blessed One: ‘But, venerable sir, how is it when one who possesses right view does not fall away from it after death, when the body breaks up? “‘Ānanda, here some person possesses confirmed confidence in the Buddha thus: “The Blessed One is accomplished, fully enlightened, perfect in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of worlds, incomparable leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, enlightened, blessed. He possesses confirmed confidence in the Dhamma thus: “The Dhamma is well expounded by the Blessed One, directly visible, immediate, inviting one to come and see, applicable, to be personally experienced by the wise. He possesses confirmed confidence in the Saṅgha thus: “The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practising the good way, practising the straight way, practising the true way, practising the proper way; that is, the four pairs of persons, the eight types of individuals—this Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world. He possesses the virtues dear to the noble ones, unbroken, untorn, unblemished, unmottled, freeing, praised by the wise, ungrasped, leading to concentration. It is in such a way, Ānanda, that one who possesses right view does not fall away from it after death, when the body breaks up. 1081. “When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda asked the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, how is it when one who possesses right view falls away from it after death, when the body breaks up? “‘Ānanda, here some person does not possess confirmed confidence in the Buddha … nor does he possess the virtues dear to the noble ones … It is in such a way, Ānanda, that one who possesses right view falls away from it after death, when the body breaks up. 1082. “When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda asked the Blessed One: ‘But, venerable sir, how is it when one who possesses right view neither falls away from it nor does not fall away from it after death, when the body breaks up? “‘Ānanda, here some person possesses confirmed confidence in the Buddha … He possesses the virtues dear to the noble ones … But he has not made the breakthrough to the Dhamma, has not attained the deathless goal, and has not awakened to the unsurpassed security from bondage. Yet he has developed the four jhānas that constitute the higher mind and are pleasant dwellings in this very life, and he has realized for himself with direct knowledge, here and now, the five lower fetters that have been abandoned.
